details: The cryptocurrency market experienced a significant downturn on November 5, 2026, with Bitcoin falling over 5% to approximately $75,880 and Ethereum tumbling over 7% to $2,233. This decline wiped out gains from a post-election rally and coincided with a broad sell-off in U.S. technology stocks, particularly those related to artificial intelligence. Over $1 billion in leveraged cryptocurrency positions were liquidated across the market, primarily long positions, indicating a broad retreat from riskier assets and concerns about elevated valuations in tech.
title: Crypto Market Erases Election Rally Amid Wall Street Tech Sell-off

details: The National Bank of Ukraine announced on November 5, 2026, its opposition to the current draft of crypto bill No. 10225-d. The central bank cited risks to monetary sovereignty, financial stability, and insufficient oversight of foreign tokens as reasons for its stance, pushing for revisions before a final parliamentary vote.
title: Ukraine Central Bank Opposes Crypto Bill Citing Monetary Risks

details: A new report from Polaris Market Research, released on November 5, 2026, projects the global stablecoins and CBDCs market to grow from $32.24 billion in 2025 to $409.57 billion by 2034, with a CAGR of 32.7%. This significant growth is attributed to increasing regulatory clarity through frameworks like the GENIUS Act and MiCA, which are encouraging banks and traditional financial institutions to adopt digital currencies for payments, settlement, and remittances.
sourceName: PR Newswire (reporting Polaris Market Research findings)
title: Stablecoins & CBDCs Market Projected to Reach $409.57 Billion by 2034
